carles_method.description: Jean Carles' systematic perfume construction method
carles_method.principle: Systematically trial combinations of characteristic materials against base types using a grid approach

positions.effets: Top note modifiers — sparkle and lift (aldehydes, citrus, green)
positions.modificateurs: Heart note modifiers — character and theme
positions.fond: Base note foundation — longevity and depth

method_steps: 1. Choose a characterizing material (the star ingredient)
2. Build a base accord (amber, woody, musk, or chypre)
3. Trial the star against multiple bases in a grid
5. Add modifiers (top note sparkle, heart bridges)

roudnitska_roles.description: Edmond Roudnitska's aesthetic role taxonomy for perfume materials
roudnitska_roles.principle: Every material in a composition serves an aesthetic function, not just a scent category

transparence.description: Materials that give airy, lifted, abstract quality — 'open the window'
transparence.effect: Prevents composition from feeling heavy or closed

chaleur.description: Materials that provide warmth and comfort
chaleur.effect: Creates psychological warmth and enveloping quality

noblesse.description: Materials that convey quality and refinement

peau.effect: Creates close-to-skin effect and personal aura

eclat.description: Materials that create brightness and radiance

profondeur.description: Materials that create depth and mystery
profondeur.effect: Adds complexity and intrigue to dry-down

opk_sar.description: Ohloff, Pickenhagen & Kraft Structure-Activity Relationship principles
opk_sar.principle: Molecular structure determines olfactory character — predictable patterns exist

rules.detail: C8=orange, C9=rose, C10=waxy-orange, C11=clean-waxy, C12=metallic-soapy. Each CH₂ shifts from fruity→waxy→soapy→metallic.
Odd-carbon aldehydes are more floral, even-carbon more fatty/waxy
Branched aldehydes (e.g., C12 MNA) are softer and less harsh than linear counterparts

rules.rule: Ionone ring size determines violet vs iris
rules.detail: Alpha-ionone = more violet-like, beta-ionone = more woody-iris. Methyl substitution adds powdery warmth.

rules.rule: Macrocyclic ring size determines musk character
rules.detail: C14-C16 macrolides = sweet, skin-like musk. Smaller rings = sharper. Larger = weaker.
Esters with bulky R groups are more stable. Linear esters hydrolyze faster.
Higher CLP (Clog P) = more lipophilic = slower evaporation = longer lasting on skin
Higher VP = more volatile = more projection but less longevity

rules.rule: Molecular weight correlates with note position
rules.detail: MW < 170 = top note, 170-250 = heart, >250 = base. Exceptions exist for cyclic structures.

jellinek_map.description: Paul Jellinek's psychological odor effect map with dual axes
jellinek_map.principle: Odors affect psychology along two orthogonal axes — can map any material to a quadrant
jellinek_map.design_principle: A well-balanced composition should have materials spanning at least 2-3 quadrants for complexity. Monotone compositions (all in one quadrant) lack depth.

key_principles: Molecular geometry determines smell — small structural changes create large olfactory shifts
Olfactory receptors are combinatorial — each molecule activates a unique pattern of receptors
The 'perfume pyramid' is an approximation — actual temporal evolution depends on vapor pressure curves
Fixation is both physical (molecular trapping) and perceptual (receptor adaptation masking base notes)
Fragrance families are defined by dominant accord, not individual materials
Balance requires tension — purely harmonious compositions are boring
The best perfumes have a 'twist' — one unexpected element that creates memorability
Systematic grid trials (Carles method) outperform random experimentation

perfume_materials_natural_origin.source: Perfume & Flavor Materials of Natural Origin (Arctander)
key_principles: Natural materials are complex mixtures — a single EO can contain 200+ molecules
The 'body' of a natural material comes from trace components, not the major ones
Synthetic materials should reconstruct the olfactory profile, not just the chemical composition
Tenacity depends on the molecular weight distribution, not just a single molecule's MW
